To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the requirements generation process should consist of the following activities: requirements elicitation, requirements analysis, requirements validation, and requirements verification; (ii) the requirements generation activities can be implemented and executed more effectively by mapping popular methods to lower level activity objectives; and (iii) the selection of appropriate requirements generation methods can be optimized using selection criteria that are mapped to the activity objectives.

we have defined an effective model for the requirements generation process, identified objectives for the activities in our model, mapped popular methods to the lower level activities, and provided a criterion-based process for optimizing method selections.
